method: In the first session,  I learnd the method practical research. And in the second session, our tutor let us use this method. He guided us to manually install VSCode and set up a GitHub step by step.
related_work: This week I also read Christiane Paul's Digital Art (3rd ed., Thames & Hudson, 2015) and Campbell-Kelly et al.'s Computer: A History of the Information Machine (4th ed., Routledge, 2023). I also watched The Net Ninja's HTML & CSS Crash Course on YouTube. I have not finished reading them, but these three sources significantly strengthened my understanding of digital art, computing history, and web coding.

conclusion_future_work: To solve how code drives images into an interactive webpage, I will review Blackboard materials and ask technician Alice. In practice, I will use HTML to make my pixel art clickable, turning flashlight assets into an interactive page step by step by myself.
results_discussion: This week, I completed two drawing tasks. For Figure 1 which made on Thursday, I photographed myself with a 3D printer in Capital House and edited myself onto it, pretending I was being printed. For Figure 2, I drew a half-mechanical headless lamb. We need to draw classmates, and I guess maybe we don`t need to draw the real human. So I combine my group member`s love for robots and a fantasy lamb game to create this amazing animal. I also prepared Project 0 assets. I split a flashlight into bulb, circuit, switch, and shell, then drew pixel art for each part. However, I am still unsure how to turn these assets into an interactive webpage and how to embed the code. This remains my key challenge.
